course_name_original: Measurement and Control Systems in Smart Grids
course_name_en: Measurement and Control Systems in Smart Grids

learning_outcomes.text: Knows and understands the operating principle of measurement systems and control of energy and technological processes.
Knows the basics of designing measurement and control systems in Smart Grids.
Knows and understands the principles of cooperation between hardware and software elements of measurement systems.
Is able to program applications for data collection, inference, and process visualization.
Is able to design a measurement and control scheme for a selected technological process.
Is able to build control algorithms for power processes using the SCADA system.
Is able to constructively cooperate in a group solving assigned laboratory tasks.
Is aware of the importance of professional conduct, adherence to professional ethics, and respect for diversity of views and cultures.

syllabus_topics: Construction and management of measurement and control systems in Smart Grids
Systems for monitoring the course of technological or production processes.
Measurements, monitoring, and security in Smart Grid systems.
BigData analysis of large data sets.
Renewable energy as a controllable source.
Distributed systems and microgrids and energy clusters.
zenon – Tool for monitoring, control, visualization, and supervision of systems.
zenon – Most important elements of the project structure.
zenon – Execution and configuration of a new project.
zenon – Visualization of values and limits.
assessment_rules: The final grade is determined as: final grade = test grade x 0.4 + laboratory grade x 0.6. Students are assessed for tasks performed during laboratory classes. The condition for passing is attendance at laboratory classes and obtaining a positive grade from these classes, with a minimum test result of 50%. More than one unjustified absence results in failing the course. If exercises are passed on a retake date, the final grade is the arithmetic mean of all previous grades, with a minimum grade of 3.0 awarded.
